html:
A large dam and hydroelectric power station on the Danube where the river cuts through the Carpathian mountains at the Iron Gates gorge, on the border between Romania and Serbia. It was built jointly by Romania and Yugoslavia from 1964 to 1972.

The gorge had long been the most dangerous stretch of the Danube, with rapids and rocks that slowed shipping. The dam tamed it and made it navigable through big locks on both sides, and its power plant became one of the largest in Europe. The two countries, one in the Soviet bloc and one outside it, shared the cost and the power equally.

The reservoir drowned old towns and villages. Among them was Ada Kaleh, an island with a Turkish community, a mosque and an old fortress, whose people were resettled. Roman remains from Trajan's road and bridge works in the gorge were moved or lost, though the carved Tabula Traiana was raised above the water. A second dam, Iron Gate II, was finished downstream in the 1980s.
